newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Electric begins work on 600-megawatt plant.
newsitem.headline: Israel Electric begins work on 600-megawatt plant.

text.p: State-owned Israel Electric Corp said on Wednesday it had begun construction of a 600-megawatt power plant in central Israel.
The company said that in the first phase it would install two 150-megawatt turbines at Gezer, 15 km (nine miles) east of Tel Aviv, at a cost of $300 million.

Plans call for two additional turbines to be installed within the next few years, bringing capacity up to 600 megawatts. The company said it hoped eventually to produce as much as 2,500 megawatts at the plant.
A company spokeswoman said plans to reach full capacity would only occur "sometime in the future".
The first unit at Gezer will begin generating electricity in 1998.
The Gezer turbines will run on diesel fuel until Israel begins importing natural gas, at which time they will switch over. Natural gas imports are expected to begin in the year 2000.
At present, the company's seven large plants and several smaller facilities have a total capacity of 7,500 megawatts.
Israel Electric has turned to the international financial markets to help raise a portion of its $1.5 billion, five-year development programme to build power plants and other infrastructure.
